passage: In some valleys, elk feed heavily on young willow trees that grow along streams. An ecologist hypothesizes that when wolves returned to one such valley, willows there grew taller because the wolves reduced how much elk fed near the streams.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the ecologist's hypothesis?
choices: After wolves returned, elk spent less time near streams, and the willows there grew taller than before.
Willows also grew taller in nearby valleys without wolves, because of several unusually wet years.
Before wolves returned, there were more elk in the valley than in most of the surrounding areas.
The wolves in the valley hunted mainly in winter, when the willow trees have no leaves to eat.
steps: The hypothesis is a chain: wolves → elk avoid streams → willows grow taller.
The best support shows both links: elk spending less time near streams and willows growing taller.
Taller willows in valleys without wolves would weaken the hypothesis; elk numbers before and wolves' hunting season don't test the chain.
key: For a cause-and-effect chain, the best evidence shows each link.
